summary: The Hong Kong PhD Fellowship Scheme (HKPFS) is a Research Grants Council (RGC) programme, set up in 2009, to attract top students from around the world to full-time PhD study at Hong Kong's UGC-funded universities. Applicants register with the RGC and also apply to the university; the university nominates its best candidates and the RGC decides. A fellowship pays a monthly stipend and a yearly conference and research travel allowance for up to three years, and the universities add their own support. 400 fellowships will be awarded in 2027/28.
eligibility_notes:
Open to candidates seeking admission as new full-time PhD students at one of eight UGC-funded universities in Hong Kong: City University of Hong Kong, Hong Kong Baptist University, Lingnan University, The Chinese University of Hong Kong, The Education University of Hong Kong, The Hong Kong Polytechnic University, The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology and The University of Hong Kong. Eligibility does not depend on country of origin, prior work experience or ethnic background.

Applicants must meet the admission requirements of the university and programme they choose; those are set by each university. Programme eligibility is a matter for the university.

Someone already doing a PhD may apply for another PhD as a new full-time student; the Selection Panel decides whether the earlier PhD study is discounted. Applicants without all transcripts or test results yet are encouraged to apply if their record is strong, and universities may give conditional offers.

English: IELTS or TOEFL is required for applicants from non-English-speaking universities unless they show English was the language of instruction; it is not needed for non-English-medium programmes such as Chinese-language ones. Other test requirements depend on the university. PolyU requires valid English test results or proof of English as the language of instruction at the time of submission.

Selection criteria: academic excellence is the primary consideration, together with research ability and potential, communication and interpersonal skills, and leadership abilities. Universities may add attributes (PolyU also lists cultural diversity and societal responsibility; HKUST lists international exposure).

Rules for applying: only one initial application may be sent to the RGC, and several applications lead to disqualification. Up to two programmes or departments (in one or two universities) may be chosen, with a priority. Only one HKPFS award is made per successful applicant, and a declined first-choice offer does not pass to the second choice. Applicants must disclose use of AI tools in preparing their application to the university, and meet data-management and research-integrity expectations in the Guidance Note.
age_experience_notes: No age limit and no work-experience requirement are stated. The RGC says eligibility does not depend on prior work experience.
funding_summary: The RGC fellowship pays an annual stipend of HK$344,400 (HK$28,700 per month) and an annual conference and research-related travel allowance of HK$14,400, for up to three years. Universities may give additional support for students who need more than three years, and each university adds its own package (for example tuition waiver, cash awards and hall places). The RGC page gives award values for 2026/27; the HKU, PolyU, HKUST and HKBU pages show the same amounts for 2027/28.
programmes_note: Full-time PhD programmes at the eight participating universities, in any field that the university offers. Shortlisted applications are assessed by one of two RGC selection panels: Sciences, Medicine, Engineering and Technology; or Humanities, Social Sciences and Business Studies. Programme information and requirements are on each university's own page, linked from the RGC participating-universities page. HKUST says its PhD takes three years with a relevant research master's, or four years with a bachelor's.
institutions_note: Eight UGC-funded universities take part (listed in the eligibility section). The applicant chooses up to two programmes or departments at one or two of them, lists the preferred university first, and cannot change the choices after the RGC deadline. If two universities nominate the same applicant, the RGC processes the nomination from the university the applicant ranked first. If two programmes in the same university are chosen, that university decides which one it nominates.

summary.detail: Full-time PhD at one of the eight UGC-funded universities. RGC award: HK$344,400 stipend a year and HK$14,400 a year conference and travel allowance, for up to three years. Normative PhD length depends on the university (HKUST: 3 years after a relevant research master's, 4 years after a bachelor's).

benefits.limit_text: HK$344,400 a year (HK$28,700 per month) stipend from the RGC
benefits.conditions: Up to three years from the RGC. Universities may add support for a fourth year (HKU, Lingnan, HKUST, HKBU and EdUHK describe fourth-year or four-year support).

benefits.limit_text: Conference and research-related travel allowance of HK$14,400 a year
benefits.conditions: Up to three years from the RGC (HKUST and HKBU describe four years / three years in their packages).

benefits.limit_text: University package: tuition fee waiver (HKU composition fee waiver HK$49,500 a year; CUHK tuition fee waiver up to HK$198,000; PolyU Research Excellence Scholarship as tuition waiver; HKUST four years; HKBU four years)
benefits.conditions: Provided by the university for the normative study period, not by the RGC. EdUHK gives a one-year fee waiver for the fourth year of a four-year PhD.

benefits.limit_text: University cash award: HKU, PolyU, HKUST: HK$40,000 in year 1, then HK$20,000 a year; CUHK lodging award up to HK$100,000 (HK$40,000 first year, HK$20,000 later); HKBU Elite Scholar Award HK$40,000 a year for three years; HKBU Research Support Fund HK$25,000 over four years
benefits.conditions: Provided by each university and subject to its conditions (for example satisfactory progress at HKBU).

benefits.limit_text: Guaranteed university accommodation: HKU guaranteed hall place in year 1 (renewable); PolyU 2 years; CUHK first-year hostel fee waiver and guaranteed on-campus place; HKUST first year; HKBU shared-room housing for the first 2 years; EdUHK on-campus housing for the normative period
benefits.conditions: Varies by university, subject to hall policies and on-time hall application and registration.

requirements.text: Initial application in the RGC HKPFS Electronic System, completed in English (except the Chinese name field). It has four sections: personal particulars; choice of universities and programmes (up to two); authorisation and declaration; source of information. Submission generates a Reference Number (format PF26-xxxxx) and a login password sent by email. The system times out after 30 minutes idle.

Full application to each chosen university through its own online system, quoting the HKPFS Reference Number, by the university deadline. An initial application not followed by a full application is void. Universities may charge an application fee; the RGC charges none.

Academic transcripts and degree certificates as the university requires (for example PolyU asks you to list and upload proof of every qualification, prize, publication, activity, employment and training, with official English translations for non-English documents).
Valid English language test result (IELTS or TOEFL), or proof that English was the language of instruction.
requirements.conditional_rule: Applicants from non-English-speaking universities; not needed for non-English-medium programmes such as Chinese-language ones. Other test rules depend on the university.

requirements.text: Research plan, past research experience and vision statement as the university asks (PolyU makes 'Part C Research Plan and Vision Statement' compulsory). The RGC asks universities to assess academic excellence, research ability and potential, communication and interpersonal skills, and leadership.

Academic referee reports through the university system. No referees are needed at the RGC initial stage. PolyU asks for two academic referees who know your work (not the proposed supervisor, not non-academics) and advises getting their consent first. HKUST asks referees to submit by 8 December 2026 where possible.
Disclosure of any AI tools used in preparing the application (models or tools, purpose, extent), given to the university.

application_steps.title: Send one initial application to the RGC
application_steps.detail: Open from 1 September 2026 (12:00 noon HKT). Use the RGC HKPFS Electronic System, choose up to two programmes or departments with a priority, and read the Guidance Note first. Submit by 1 December 2026, 12:00 noon Hong Kong time; late submissions are not considered. Only one initial application is allowed. Choices can be changed until the deadline, not after.

application_steps.title: Apply to each chosen university with your Reference Number
application_steps.detail: After getting the HKPFS Reference Number, send a full application to each chosen university and programme before its deadline, quoting the number. All eight universities close at 11:59 pm Hong Kong time on 1 December 2026 (HKU's page says both steps by 12:00 noon that day, so apply early). Use a separate application for each programme where the university asks for that. Pay any university application fee. If you leave out the number your application is treated as a regular application with no HKPFS consideration.

application_steps.title: University assessment and interview
application_steps.detail: Universities check your full application, usually hold interviews (for example CUHK interviews shortlisted applicants from September to December 2026), and nominate selected candidates to the RGC. Data in the RGC form is cross-checked with the university application. Applicants nominated but not given an HKPFS may still be admitted for regular PhD study and may be offered a studentship or other support.

application_steps.title: RGC selection panels decide
application_steps.detail: Shortlisted nominations are reviewed by one of two panels (Sciences, Medicine, Engineering and Technology; Humanities, Social Sciences and Business Studies), using academic excellence as the primary criterion plus research ability, communication and leadership.

application_steps.title: Results are announced in May 2027
application_steps.detail: The RGC notifies only successful applicants, by email and letter, and announces results in May 2027 on its website. The decision is final and the RGC gives no feedback to individual applicants. (CUHK says it expects to notify outcomes from March to April 2027; PolyU says the RGC announces in April to May 2027.)

application_steps.title: Accept and register at the university
application_steps.detail: Registration is normally between July and September 2027. Deferral to 31 January 2028 at the latest is possible with justified reasons and RGC approval. Apply for a student visa or entry permit through the Immigration Department process. Awardees must remain a full-time PhD student at the university named in the offer letter; changing university ends the fellowship.

application_steps.title: Study full-time and keep the university conditions
application_steps.detail: The RGC stipend and travel allowance run for up to three years; university packages add tuition waiver, cash awards, and hall places subject to each university's rules and progress conditions. Universities may add support for a fourth year.
